questions.q: In the chapter's intent-based model, a scheduled job is formalized as a tuple of:
options: command, cron expression, timezone, owner, notification list
Job = (work_unit, preconditions, constraints, priority, estimated_cost)
Job = (name, schedule, retry count, timeout, alert channel)
script path, SQL Agent job name, step count, proxy account, history retention
questions.explain: The chapter formalizes a job as (work_unit, preconditions, constraints, priority, estimated_cost) — intent encoded as signals, not a fixed calendar entry.

questions.q: How does the chapter tier signal collection frequency?
options: High-frequency signals (connections, CPU) sampled every 10–15 seconds into a ring buffer; lower-frequency signals every 1–5 minutes; expensive signals on-demand or hourly and cached
Every signal sampled once per second regardless of cost
All signals collected daily at 2 AM by a single job
Only semantic signals are collected; real-time metrics come from the OS
questions.explain: The tiered model samples high-frequency signals every 10–15s, lower-frequency ones every 1–5 min, and expensive ones (bloat, fragmentation analysis) on-demand or hourly.

questions.q: The signal collection procedure reads CPU utilization from which SQL Server source?
options: sys.dm_os_performance_counters with counter_name = 'Processor Time'
sys.dm_os_sys_info directly for the cpu_ticks column
The RING_BUFFER_SCHEDULER_MONITOR ring buffer in sys.dm_os_ring_buffers, extracting ProcessUtilization from the XML record
An external WMI query against the Windows host
questions.explain: CollectSchedulerSignals queries sys.dm_os_ring_buffers for ring_buffer_type RING_BUFFER_SCHEDULER_MONITOR and parses the SystemHealth/ProcessUtilization XML value.

questions.q: How is the workload forecast built that the scheduler uses to anticipate execution windows?
options: A fixed calendar of holidays entered manually each quarter
168 hour-of-week buckets holding the 75th percentile of the last 30 days of connection and CPU signal history, rebuilt nightly
A simple 7-day moving average of total batch requests
The DBA's own estimate of quiet hours recorded in a configuration table
questions.explain: build_workload_forecast computes the 75th percentile per hour-of-week bucket (168 buckets) from 30 days of signal history and rebuilds it nightly.

questions.q: When multiple eligible jobs compete, how does the conflict resolver decide which run?
options: It runs the job that was created first, FIFO order
It picks one job at random to avoid starvation

It calculates the combined estimated cost of eligible jobs sorted by priority and selects a maximal subset whose aggregate I/O and CPU estimates stay within configurable limits, deferring the rest with a logged reason
It runs all eligible jobs concurrently and lets Resource Governor sort it out
questions.explain: The resolver selects a maximal subset of priority-sorted eligible jobs whose aggregate estimated I/O and CPU fit within limits; jobs that don't fit are deferred with a deferred_reason.
